newsitem.title: BURUNDI: U.N. refugee chief says security better in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: U.N. refugee chief says security better in Burundi.

text.p: U.N. refugee agency chief Sadako Ogata said on Tuesday security appeared to be improving in Burundi but was not good enough to repatriate Burundian refugees in Tanzania and Zaire.

"My visit here was only one day so it is difficult to give a general impression but I have the impression that that security is almost total, security is almost re-established and the objective of the government is to re-establish security," Ogata, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, told reporters.
"The president indicated to me that his objective was to re-establish security and he also explained his determination to reach this goal," said Ogata, who is Japanese but was speaking French.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the assassination of its first freely-elected Hutu president in 1993.

The civilian government was overthrown in an army coup last July. Military ruler Pierre Buyoya, under the pressure of regional sanctions against his tiny country, has promised peace talks with Hutu rebel groups but they have failed to start.
The U.N. human rights office said on January 29 the army had killed at least 1,000 people in the seven weeks to January 21 in a new escalation of violence in the three-year-old civil war.
President Buyoya promised to investigate the U.N. report.
Tanzania has an estimated 240,000 Burundian Hutu refugees while another 46,000 are believed to remain in Zaire, scattered by fighting between rebels and government troops since October.
Last month the Burundian army admitted killing 126 Burundian refugees forced home by authorities in Tanzania following the return of some 500,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees to their homeland.
"Our goal is for a better situation, that it should be totally stable so we could say we would organise repatriation for everybody in every province," Ogata said on Monday.
"I don't think we are yet there but I hope that we will arrive at this reality soon," she added.
She said every Burundian minister she had met had expressed regret at the killing of the returning refugees last month.
She said the government clearly felt that the expulsion of the refugees by Tanzania was no excuse to kill them but she hoped soldiers on the ground would receive the same message.
Ogata later on Tuesday flew to neighbouring Rwanda, where she said former Rwandan Hutu troops were probably benefitting from food aid given to Rwandan refugees trapped with them in eastern Zaire.
